status.detail: Editor keeps a unique 11-zone Priority Grid preview, but the runtime path falls back to plain Grid for the same zone count.

next_action.label: Approve the implementation-grade design
next_action.reason: Exact files, symbols, steps, tests, and risks are now captured in the artifact.

actions.label: Design fix
actions.note: Dashboard-only action. No upstream comment or PR is posted by this artifact update.

design.root_cause: FancyZones runtime has an off-by-one guard in LayoutConfigurator::PriorityGrid. The editor keeps a dedicated 11-zone template (_priorityData has 11 entries and GridLayoutModel.InitPriorityGrid uses <=), but the runtime checks zoneCount < predefinedLayoutsCount. With predefinedLayoutsCount == 11, zoneCount == 11 incorrectly falls through to Grid(), so the applied layout diverges from the editor preview.
evidence: GridLayoutModel._priorityData contains 11 hard-coded Priority Grid templates, and GridLayoutModel.InitPriorityGrid reloads them when TemplateZoneCount <= _priorityData.Length.
LayoutConfigurator.cpp comments say PriorityGrid is unique for zoneCount <= 11, but LayoutConfigurator::PriorityGrid currently uses if (zoneCount < predefinedLayoutsCount).
For zoneCount == 11, predefinedLayoutsCount is 11, so the runtime returns Grid(workArea, zoneCount, spacing) instead of predefinedPriorityGridLayouts[10].
Issue #28672 and the 2026-07-31 comment both report that 11-zone Priority Grid previews correctly in the editor but applies like a regular grid at runtime.

affected_files.purpose: Runtime layout selection for Priority Grid vs regular Grid.
Editor-side source of truth for Priority Grid templates and preview behavior.
New runtime regression test covering the 11-zone Priority Grid boundary.
Editor regression that locks the 11-zone template shape used by the preview.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Runtime uses the predefined Priority Grid table only when zoneCount < predefinedLayoutsCount, so 11 zones incorrectly fall through to Grid().
implementation_steps.change: Make the boundary inclusive so zoneCount == 11 also uses predefinedPriorityGridLayouts[10], matching the editor and the file comment.
edge_cases: Keep zoneCount <= 0 returning an empty map.
Keep zoneCount > 11 using Grid() exactly as today.
Do not change spacing handling or layout math for the existing 1-10 templates.
tests: Add a runtime unit test for zoneCount == 11.
Add/keep a guard that zoneCount == 12 still falls back to Grid().

implementation_steps.current_behavior: There is no runtime regression test covering the 11-zone Priority Grid boundary, so the off-by-one can drift unnoticed.
implementation_steps.change: Add a focused C++ unit test that builds a known work area, calls LayoutConfigurator::PriorityGrid(..., 11, ...), and asserts the resulting zone geometry or adjacency matches the 11th predefined template rather than a uniform grid fallback.
implementation_steps.code_block: auto zones = LayoutConfigurator::PriorityGrid(workArea, 11, 0);\nAssert::AreEqual(static_cast<size_t>(11), zones.size());\n// Assert center/topology from predefinedPriorityGridLayouts[10], not Grid(..., 11, ...).
edge_cases: Use a deterministic work area so integer rounding is stable.
Add a companion assertion that 12 zones still use regular Grid behavior.
Prefer topology/zone-span assertions over brittle pixel-perfect values where possible.
tests: Run any adjacent Priority Grid runtime unit tests in the same test binary.

implementation_steps.current_behavior: Editor correctness is implicit; there is no explicit unit test pinning the 11-zone Priority Grid template that the runtime must match.
implementation_steps.change: Add a small editor regression that instantiates a Priority Grid with 11 zones and asserts the resulting rows/columns/cell-child map reflect the dedicated 11-zone template, preventing future drift between editor and runtime expectations.
implementation_steps.code_block: var model = new GridLayoutModel(\"Priority Grid\", LayoutType.PriorityGrid) { ZoneCount = 11 };\n// Force init/reload if needed.\nCollectionAssert.AreEqual(expectedCellChildMap, Flatten(model.CellChildMap));
edge_cases: Assert the dedicated 11-zone pattern, not just zone count.
Keep the test resilient to harmless percentage rounding differences by checking topology before exact percents where appropriate.
tests: Keep existing GridLayoutModel validity tests passing.

verify: Build FancyZones runtime: pwsh .\\tools\\build\\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\\src\\modules\\FancyZones\\FancyZonesLib\\FancyZonesLib.vcxproj
Build FancyZones C++ unit tests: pwsh .\\tools\\build\\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\\src\\modules\\FancyZones\\FancyZonesTests\\UnitTests\\UnitTests.vcxproj
Build FancyZones editor unit tests: pwsh .\\tools\\build\\build.ps1 -Platform x64 -Configuration Debug -Path .\\src\\modules\\FancyZones\\FancyZonesEditor.UnitTests\\FancyZonesEditor.UnitTests.csproj
Run the focused C++ unit test with vstest.console.exe against the FancyZones UnitTests binary and a filter for PriorityGrid_ElevenZones_UsesPredefinedLayout.
Run the focused editor test with vstest.console.exe against FancyZonesEditor.UnitTests.dll and a filter for PriorityGrid11ZonesUsesDedicatedTemplate.
Manual E2E: create/edit an 11-zone Priority Grid in the editor, save/apply it, then confirm the applied layout spans the same center/priority zones shown in the editor preview.
risks: This changes runtime behavior for every saved/applied 11-zone Priority Grid, so persisted layouts that accidentally relied on the bug will visibly change.
Geometry assertions can be sensitive to rounding; tests should prefer topology where possible.
Any hidden divergence between editor and runtime data beyond the boundary check will surface once the runtime starts honoring the 11th template.
alternatives: Changing the editor to fall back at 10 zones would preserve the bug and contradict both the issue report and the runtime comment that says Priority Grid is unique through 11 zones.
Leaving behavior as-is and documenting it would not match user expectations or the editor preview.
Using the regular Grid for all high counts avoids the branch entirely, but it would intentionally remove the 11-zone template that already exists in the editor.
